text: APPROVE. The extracted `IsInterpreterDirective` keeps the same condition (`prefix == "#"`, bounds check, then `line[i + 1] == '!'`) and the ternary returns `-1` or `i` exactly as the old `if`/`return` did. Replacing the nested `if` with a ternary costs the same nesting increment but drops the `&&` sequence, taking complexity from 16 to 15. A `ReadOnlySpan<char>` parameter accepts either a string or a span argument, so the build should be unaffected, though I judged this from the diff alone and did not build it.
